key_insight: Jointly tuning reward-shaping parameters and DQN hyperparameters is essential to break local minima in non-holonomic control tasks like autonomous parking.
engineering_relevance: The proposed reward design and meta-optimization workflow offer a practical path to more reliable self-parking controllers with smoother, safer maneuvers.
method: Coverage-gated alignment feedback to guide the car only when alignment is meaningful
Drive-direction switch regularization to penalize unnecessary reversals
Aligned episode termination plus surrogate-based Bayesian optimization for co-optimizing reward and DQN settings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on an autonomous parallel parking task, where the co-optimized DQN outperformed uncalibrated baselines in both success rate and trajectory smoothness.
watch_item: Because performance depends on coupled reward and algorithm settings, the approach may be sensitive to transfer across vehicles, parking layouts, or simulator-to-real deployment.
paper_title: Optimal Reward Shaping: Autonomous Car Parking Case Study
